title: Section 84 — Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman

content.overview: BNS s. 84 — Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman. BNS restatement of IPC 498. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 498. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 84 is the rule on “Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman”. The section provides that whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of any other man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or detains with that intent any such woman, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 84 exists so that “Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. learningObjectives: Understand the statutory scope of enticing, taking away, concealing, or detaining a married woman under BNS s. 84.
Analyze the mental element requiring knowledge or reason to believe that the woman is the wife of another man.
Examine the specific intent required: that she may have illicit intercourse with any person.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 84 penalizes whoever takes or entices away any woman who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of any other man, with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person, or conceals or detains with that intent any such woman, punishable with imprisonment up to two years, fine, or both.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes the intentional taking, enticing, or detention of a married woman for the purpose of illicit intercourse.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 84 (corresponding to IPC s. 498).
Actus reus: Taking away, enticing away, concealing, or detaining a married woman.
Mens rea: Knowledge or reason to believe she is married, with intent that she have illicit intercourse.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to two years, or fine, or both.
essentialIngredients: The woman is the wife of another man.
The accused knew or had reason to believe she was the wife of another man.
The accused took away, enticed away, concealed, or detained her.
The act was done with intent that she may have illicit intercourse with any person.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 84 carries forward the provisions of Section 498 of the Indian Penal Code. The provision penalizes four distinct acts regarding a married woman: taking away, enticing away, concealing, or detaining her. The accused must possess knowledge or reason to believe that the woman is lawfully married to another man. The specific mens rea required is the intent that she may engage in illicit intercourse with the accused or any other person. 'Enticing' implies an inducement or allure that operates on the woman's mind to leave her husband's custody or protection.
examples: Teaching example (Enticing a married woman): An accused, knowing a woman is married and residing with her husband, offers her money and promises of shelter to persuade her to leave her husband's home to engage in sexual relations with him. This constitutes enticing under s. 84.

Teaching example (Voluntary departure without inducement): A married woman leaves her husband's home entirely on her own accord due to domestic friction and later seeks lodging at a friend's house. Without proof of enticing, taking, or detaining by the friend, s. 84 is not attracted.
distinctions: Section 84 vs Section 87 (Kidnapping/abduction of woman): Section 87 requires kidnapping or abduction by force or deceit; Section 84 can be satisfied by mere enticement of a married woman.

Section 84 vs Adultery jurisprudence: While criminal adultery was struck down under constitutional law, s. 84 specifically targets the predatory taking, enticing, or detention of a married woman for illicit intercourse.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who hid a married woman in his farmhouse against her family's inquiries to facilitate sexual relations with his associates is liable under s. 84.
Rule: Concealing or detaining a known married woman with intent that she have illicit intercourse completes the offence under BNS s. 84.
Application: The accused knew she was married and actively concealed her whereabouts for illicit purposes.
Conclusion: The accused is guilty of an offence under BNS s. 84.
